topics.title: Accessible Naming, Landmarks & Source Order
topics.summary: Go beyond basic semantics by reasoning about accessible names, landmark labels, keyboard order, and how DOM source order affects users.

concepts.name: Accessible names
concepts.explanation: Controls need a reliable name from visible text, label, alt, aria-label, or aria-labelledby. Prefer visible native labels when possible.

concepts.name: Landmark labels
concepts.explanation: When several nav or region landmarks exist, label them so users can distinguish “Primary navigation” from “Course navigation”.

concepts.name: Source order
concepts.explanation: Keyboard and screen-reader navigation generally follow DOM order. Avoid using CSS to create a visual order that contradicts the logical reading order.

topics.example:
Home

Progress
topics.challenge: Create two nav landmarks with distinct accessible labels and one section labelled by its heading.
topics.hint: Use aria-label on repeated nav landmarks and aria-labelledby to connect a section with an existing visible heading.

topics.title: Embedded Content & Sandboxed Frames
topics.summary: Embed external documents deliberately and restrict capabilities when third-party content does not need full trust.

concepts.name: iframe
concepts.explanation: iframe embeds another browsing context. Always give important frames a useful title so assistive technology can identify them.

concepts.name: sandbox
concepts.explanation: sandbox removes capabilities from framed content until specific tokens are granted. Add only the permissions the embedded content actually needs.

concepts.name: Loading and privacy
concepts.explanation: loading="lazy" can defer off-screen frames. referrerpolicy can control what referrer information is sent to the embedded resource.

topics.example:
<iframe
  src="practice-preview.html"
  title="Practice preview"
  loading="lazy"
  sandbox="allow-scripts"
  referrerpolicy="no-referrer">
</iframe>
topics.challenge: Create an iframe with a title, lazy loading, and a sandbox attribute.
topics.hint: Start from the most restricted sandbox and add permissions only when the embedded page needs them.
topics.solution:
<iframe
  src="practice-preview.html"
  title="Practice preview"
  loading="lazy"
  sandbox="allow-scripts"
  referrerpolicy="no-referrer">
</iframe>

topics.title: Native Interactive Elements
topics.summary: Use built-in disclosure, dialog, and popover primitives before recreating their behavior with generic div elements.

concepts.name: details and summary
concepts.explanation: details creates a disclosure widget and summary supplies its label. The open attribute controls initial state.

concepts.name: dialog
concepts.explanation: dialog represents a dialog box. JavaScript can use show(), showModal(), and close(); method="dialog" forms can close a dialog with a return value.

concepts.name: Popover
concepts.explanation: The popover attribute gives lightweight top-layer behavior to ordinary elements, while popovertarget connects controls to them without a full custom widget implementation.

topics.title: Data Attributes & Machine-Readable Values
topics.summary: Attach application-specific metadata with data-* while keeping visible meaning in normal HTML and using dedicated elements for dates, measurements, and machine values.

concepts.name: data-* attributes
concepts.explanation: Custom data attributes store small pieces of application metadata on elements. JavaScript reads them through element.dataset.

concepts.name: time
concepts.explanation: time can pair human-readable text with a machine-readable datetime value, useful for dates and durations.

concepts.name: data and meter
concepts.explanation: data associates displayed content with a machine-readable value. meter represents a scalar measurement within a known range; progress represents task completion.

topics.title: Templates, Slots & Component-Friendly Markup
topics.summary: Prepare reusable DOM fragments and meaningful fallback structures that work well with JavaScript and Web Components.

concepts.name: template
concepts.explanation: template stores inert DOM content. Its children are parsed but are not rendered or executed until JavaScript clones the template content.

concepts.name: slot
concepts.explanation: Inside a shadow tree, slot defines insertion points for light-DOM content. Named slots let consumers provide different pieces of a component.

concepts.name: Fallback content
concepts.explanation: Component-friendly markup should still consider meaningful fallback content and progressive enhancement instead of assuming JavaScript always succeeds.

topics.example: HTML Intermediate
topics.challenge: Create a template containing a reusable article and demonstrate a named slot assignment on custom-element content.
topics.hint: The template itself is inert. Put the reusable markup inside it, then use slot="name" on content intended for a named slot.
topics.solution: HTML Intermediate
